To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) one-bit quantization of gradients in SGD training of speech DNs is effective and can speed up computation by a factor of 3-6, (2) AdaGrad benefits from this quantization and can give a further accuracy improvement, and (3) the combination of the above with other techniques can speed up training by a factor of up to 10.

(a) one can quantize gradients to one bit per value, and still get the same accuracy as with full precision, by carrying forward the quantization error; and (b) the combination of AdaGrad and one-bit error-feedback SGD is surprisingly effective, and leads to a small accuracy gain.

1) SGD training of DNNs can tolerate aggressive gradient quantization, 2) this enables data-parallel distributed SGD, and 3) the speed-up of data-parallel SGD scales linearly with the number of GPUs, and is independent of the minibatch size.

making SGD training of deep networks practical for large-scale data sets.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 1-bit stochastic gradient quantization is an extremely powerful and effective tool in the training of large scale deep neural networks, which allows to speedup the training process by orders of magnitude, with only small accuracy loss, or even accuracy gain.
1-bit SGD is an effective way to speed up distributed training, but it does come at the expense of a small accuracy loss, which may or may not be tolerable depending on the application.
we have developed a new distributed training method for deep neural networks that is both fast and accurate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of AdaGrad, error-feedback 1-bit quantization of the gradients, and double buffering enables us to train a 46M-parameter Switchboard DNN in 7h, and a 160M-parameter DNN in 16h, on 20 servers, with no accuracy loss.
1-bit stochastic gradient quantization is a simple and effective technique for data-parallel distributed DNN training, and that it is a promising direction for speeding up DNN training in general.
the combination of 1-bit quantization and AdaGrad enables a 10 times speedup of DNN training on GPUs.

data-parallel SGD can be used for distributed training of large DNNs with minimal loss of accuracy.
